content:
sophie: EdgeBox partner reported a spike of negative billing adjustments after the PST midnight cutover — their nightly batches appear to arrive out-of-order. Anyone able to take a look?

ken: I've seen this pattern before with another marketplace partner. Do we currently dedupe by (event_id, partner_id) only? Or do we also guard against sequence regression?

liam: We dedupe on event_id + hmac, but the delta computation uses last-seen timestamp per customer to compute usage deltas. If events arrive late but with earlier timestamps we can compute a negative delta. Partner should ideally send monotonic seq_num.

ken: example payload EdgeBox sent (sanitized):

```json
{
  "partner_id": "edgebox-01",
  "customer_id": "cust_ABC123",
  "event_id": "evt-20251112-0001",
  "seq_num": 42,
  "usage": 120,
  "timestamp": "2025-11-12T07:59:30Z",
  "signature": "hmac_sha256(...)"
}
```

ada: Can we ask them to include seq_num and publish_time in every message? That would help. In the short term we should make the ingestion tolerant: accept out-of-order events and compute delta using max(seq_num) per customer rather than last timestamp, or at least floor delta to 0.

ken: I can push a small change: if seq_num present, compute delta = usage - last_usage_by_seq[max_seq_seen]. Otherwise keep existing logic. Also add a safety floor: delta = max(delta, 0). I'll open a PR and deploy to staging.

sophie: EdgeBox confirmed they can include seq_num starting tomorrow morning. Meanwhile we have ~1.2k negative credit adjustments for cust_ABC123 and a few others. Need quick mitigation so customers don't see erroneous refunds. @ada can you coordinate comms?

billing-bot: ALERT: Reconciliation job partner-ingest created 24 negative-deltas for window 2025-11-12T00:00:00Z -> 2025-11-12T08:00:00Z (partner=edgebox-01). Ticket #INC-4478 auto-created.

ken: Pushing patch to staging now. After deploy I will run a dry-run backfill then the real backfill if results look good. Commands I'll run:

```bash
# run recon dry-run for edgebox
python tools/backfill_recon.py --partner edgebox-01 --from 2025-11-11 --to 2025-11-12 --dry-run
# then apply if dry-run OK
python tools/backfill_recon.py --partner edgebox-01 --from 2025-11-11 --to 2025-11-12 --apply --limit 500
```

liam: Note: buffering out-of-order events per-customer will increase memory on ingestion workers. I'll bump the redis cache for ingestion to 6GB and increase worker replicas from 4 -> 6 in staging so we can validate.

ada: Thanks. Sophie, please include the customer case IDs in the INC-4478 ticket and loop in EdgeBox PM. I'll draft a short partner-facing note: what we changed, why (out-of-order sequences), and recommended partner-side best practices (seq_num, immediate publish_time).

sophie: Thanks team — ken, ping here when the staging deploy is up and you run the dry-run. I'll hold on customer comms until we confirm the backfill results.
